hook: Rabinovich arrived at the Longuet-Higgins Prize, the computer vision field's highest honor for work that has stood the test of time, the same year his startup was acquired and he became CTO of a public company. His arc from Google research to Magic Leap's human-centered AR, to founding an AI meeting tool, to leading AI at one of the world's largest freelance platforms is a compressed version of the field's own evolution: from perception research to multimodal generation to enterprise deployment.
name: Andrew Rabinovich

quote.text: Special focus on Human Centered AI and Experiential Learning.

moniker: CTO and Head of AI at Upwork

reading.body:
Rabinovich's 2025 Longuet-Higgins Prize, awarded for computer vision research of lasting significance, arrived the same year his AI meeting startup completed its acquisition by Upwork, a coincidence that captures the distance the field has traveled from academic perception research to enterprise software deployment.

His trajectory runs in a single direction: from PhD-level computer vision at UC San Diego, through large-scale object detection and segmentation at Google, through human-centered perception for augmented reality at Magic Leap, to building and selling an AI meeting platform. Each move applied the previous one. The Google years produced the foundational object recognition work. Magic Leap translated that into real-time human interaction. Headroom moved the same perceptual machinery into a product layer, then into a company acquisition.

What the data does not cover is the technical architecture of any of these systems, the scale of Upwork's AI deployment, or what specifically the Longuet-Higgins committee recognized. The timeline is a career record, not a technical one. It shows a person who moved steadily from research to application to enterprise leadership, but the data says nothing about compute requirements, infrastructure decisions, or how Upwork's freelance marketplace uses the AI capabilities he now leads.
